query: An equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi high-entropy alloy has a simple solid-solution structure and favorable plasticity and machinability but relatively low hardness and strength, while its microstructure and deformation behavior remain insufficiently understood. Under hardness testing and mechanical loading of this starting state, what single intervention could overcome the strength and hardness limitation while retaining its favorable mechanical characteristics? State the proposed intervention, its mechanism, the predicted measurable change relative to the unmodified alloy, its applicable processing and test conditions, supporting prior evidence, and a microstructural and mechanical experiment that could falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Nb addition to CoCrFeNiTi high-entropy alloy can overcome the strength and hardness limitation while retaining its favorable mechanical characteristics.
generation.material_initial_state: CoCrFeNiTi high-entropy alloy with a simple solid-solution structure
generation.intervention: Addition of Nb to the alloy
generation.conditions: High-energy ball milling and discharge plasma sintering
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of Laves phase (Co2Nb-type, HCP) with Nb addition
generation.mechanism: Solid solution strengthening and precipitation of hard Laves phase
generation.predicted_outcome: Increased hardness and tensile strength with optimal balance at 5 wt% Nb addition
generation.baseline: CoCrFeNiTi high-entropy alloy without Nb addition
generation.uncertainty: Optimal Nb content for balancing strength, hardness, and plasticity

falsification_experiment.design: Tensile testing and Vickers hardness measurement
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the addition of Nb does not increase the hardness and tensile strength of the CoCrFeNiTi high-entropy alloy, the hypothesis is falsified.

Own digest: Paper card. Question: How does doping with different Nb contents (0–9 wt%) affect the microstructure, mechanical properties, and fracture behavior of CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloys prepared by high-energy ball milling and discharge plasma sintering?. System: CoCrFeNi-Nbx (x = 0, 1, 3, 5, 7, and 9 wt%) high-entropy alloys. Processing: High-energy ball milling (400 rpm, 4 h total with 10 min cooling intervals) followed by discharge plasma sintering (SPS) at 1100 °C, 30 MPa pressure, for 10 min; heating rates: 100 °C/min (0–600 °C), 50 °C/min (600–900 °C), 25 °C/min (900–1100 °C). Test conditions: Room temperature tensile testing (cross-sectional area 1.5 mm × 1 mm, tensile rate 0.2 mm/min, original gauge length 5 mm); Vickers hardness (500 g load, 15 s retention); XRD (Cu Kα, 40 kV, 40 mA, 20–90°); SEM/EDS analysis.
